items.title: D'Imperio interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2014
items.q: Louis Jordan and the Tympani Five. That was something that was sitting on the dining room table.

ctx.x: I didn’t want to be — I mean rhythm & blues was nice, you know, Louis Jordan and the Tympani Five. That was something that was sitting on the dining room table. I can’t remember all the names of the tunes, I’ve still got them there. But I mean that was Earl Bostic, all of those were swing music. But when it went into eight beat, when it started becoming [scats] that’s when I kind of lost interest in it.
Can I ask you about — I don’t think I’ve heard that term in a long time, “eight beat.”
